newsitem.title: UK: European airline Debonair plans July EASDAQ float.
newsitem.headline: European airline Debonair plans July EASDAQ float.

text.p: Debonair Holdings Plc, owner of Debonair Airways, said on Thursday it was planning to float on the EASDAQ stock market in July and pledged to create the first truly pan-European airline.
The airline, which flies six aircraft on eleven European routes, has seen its passenger numbers grow from 3,000 in its first month of operation a year ago to over 50,000 in May 1997.
Debonair was hoping to raise around 25 million stg from an institutional placing. The company is expected to be valued at around 100 million stg.
The shares are expected to be offered at between four and five pounds sterling per share.
Chairman and chief executive Franco Mancassola said Debonair would take advantage of the deregulation process in Europe's air transport industry.

New rules mean that airlines operating between European countries no longer have to return their aircraft to their home base. Carriers are also permitted to fly routes within the borders of other states.
Mancassola said by being able to operate out of more than one country it could establish itself as a low fare, "home-based" airline in many European destinations.
However, Debonair was not planning to compete directly with large airlines.
"We aim to keep below the line of competitors' radar screens," said marketing and sales director Michael Henderson.
The airline was able to pull out of unprofitable London to Newcastle and Barcelona to Madrid routes relatively cheaply because of its low fixed cost base.
New European regulations also meant that airlines no longer had to submit their range of fares for approval by government bodies, offering the opportunity for low and flexible fares.
Debonair made pre-tax losses of about 15 million stg in its first year of operation but this included the writing off of an estimated 13 million stg of development costs.
